COMPLETE_CAUSAL_CHAIN: 1. Each cli_main builds a NEW runtime pool; the previous pool's runtimes are not inherited.
3. The resident spawned by the PREVIOUS cli_main has no live owner, so it is an orphan and is REAPED -- killed deliberately.
4. The new pool then spawns a fresh resident, which pays the 211.3 s lazy weight load again.
IT_IS_DELIBERATE_NOT_A_BUG: The reaper's own comment: 'a daemon meets SIGKILL routinely - OOM kill, crash, kill -9, power loss. Measured: SIGKILLing the CLI mid-run left TWO orphaned bodies.' Reaping exists because orphaned 9.9 GB bodies leak memory. Removing it would trade a 211 s cost for a resource leak.
THEREFORE_THE_DESIGN_REQUIREMENT: A persistent resident must not be an ORPHAN. It needs to be a supervised long-lived body that the reaper recognises and spares -- an ownership record the next pool can adopt rather than reap. That is a lifetime/ownership feature, not a patch.
WHY_MY_CACHE_PATCH_COULD_NEVER_HAVE_WORK: It memoised the Python object. The child was killed by a different subsystem entirely, one whose job is to kill exactly that child.
MEASURED_PRIZE: 211.3 s per round; 6.2x on a 23-round ladder (92 min -> 15 min).
STATUS: Diagnosed to the line. NOT implemented -- adoption-instead-of-reaping is a real feature with a real failure mode (leaked bodies) and belongs in the harness with its own controls, not in a sidecar patch written at the end of a long session.
